FULL TEXT:
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP) FOR PILOT
IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PAPERLESS GUJARAT HIGH COURT
PROJECT (Developed in house under the E-`GujHC Project)
1. Purpose and Scope:
The High Court of Gujarat under the power vested in it under Article 225
lays down the SOP for pilot implementation of the paperless e filing project.
This SOP establishes the procedural framework for the pilot phase of the
Paperless E-GujHC Project. The project aims at transitioning from physical
to digital case management through AI-assisted filing and scrutiny to ensure
greater accessibility and efficiency in the administration of justice.
2. e-Filing:
2.1. Scanning Standards: Learned Advocates or Parties-in-person shall
upload clean, legible, scanned copies of case files in proper order to the
e-filing Paperless Portal developed under E-GujHC Project.
2.2. Format and Legibility: All documents must be clearly legible. As per
Rule 346 of the Gujarat High Court Rules, 1993, digital copies must
correspond page-to-page with the originals and should ideally be typed
on durable paper with a 2-inch margin before scanning.
2.3 Definition of e-File: For the purposes of this Pilot Project, any
document and set of Documents scanned and uploaded bearing the
valid physical signature of the Learned Advocate or Petitioner as the
case may be and accepted by the Registry, shall be treated as an
“e-file”.
3. Affidavits and Authenticity:
3.1. Validity of Signatures, Oaths and Affirmations: The scanned copies
of the original documents and affidavits which bear the signature of
the Learned Advocate or Petitioner, as the case may be, shall be treated
as legally valid Document for the purpose of Pilot Project.
SOP - Pilot Implementation of the Paperless Gujarat High Court Project - eGujHC Project Page 1/3
3.2. Mandatory Declaration: The authorised Advocate or Party-in-person
shall make following declaration in the prescribed format on the portal,
certifying the authenticity of the e-filed documents”
“I hereby declare that I have personally verified from
the original physical Documents and the scanned
document/file uploaded herein is a true and exact copy
of the corresponding physical originals. I further
undertake to produce the physical original before the
Hon’ble Court as and when directed or required.”
4. AI-Assisted Scrutiny and Registration:
4.1. Pre-Scrutiny: Upon submission of the e-file, the AI Software
developed under e-GujHC project will perform an automated
pre-scrutiny of the e-file to identify the office objections and display the
probable objections to the advocate or filer, who may either choose to
correct the defect or may proceed to file with objections. The system
will not block the filer to proceed with filing due to AI generated
objections.
4.2. Human Verification: A Filing Number and Registration Number shall
only be generated after Human Verification of the AI-generated
scrutiny report by the Registry’s Examiner or Verifier.
4.3. Registrar’s Authority: The Registrar or authorised Deputy/Assistant
Registrar shall have authority under Chapter II of the Gujarat High
Court Rules, 1993, to admit or refuse proceedings based on conformity
with the rules. The advocate /filer cannot claim that submission of
e-file is valid only because it is shown as valid by AI.
5. Limitation and Objections:
5.1. Effect on Limitation: The period of limitation shall continue to run
against the petitioner until all mandatory office objections are
removed and a Filing Number is generated.
5.2. Registration Number: The final Registration Number will be generated
only after the removal of all other secondary objections.
SOP - Pilot Implementation of the Paperless Gujarat High Court Project - eGujHC Project Page 2/3
5.3 Time Lines: Consistent with Rule 65 of the Gujarat High Court Rules,
1993, the advocate shall remove the objections within 15 days of
notification to avoid the matter being placed before the Court for
dismissal.
5.4 The e-file bearing registration number shall be available for the
advocates in the portal.
6. Judicial Interface and Hearings:
6.1. Hon'ble Judges’ Dashboard: Once a Registration Number is allocated,
the e-file shall be automatically synchronised and made available on
the Hon'ble Judges' Dashboard.
6.2. Valid Hearings: Any judicial hearing conducted using these e-files
shall be deemed a valid and legal hearing for all purposes of the law.
6.3. Record Preservation: In accordance with the amended Rule 164 of
the Gujarat High Court Rules, 1993, all judgments and final orders
arising from these hearings shall be permanently preserved physically
as well as digitally.
7. Legal Framework and Interpretation:
7.1. Applicability of Rules: The Gujarat High Court Rules, 1993, shall
apply to all e-filing processes mutatis mutandis.
7.2. Construction: Unless the context otherwise requires, any reference to
“e-filing” in this SOP or associated portal documentation shall be
construed as a “filing” as provided under the Gujarat High Court
Rules, 1993.
7.3 This Standard Operating Procedure will be treated as part of the
Gujarat High Court Rules, 1993.
7.4 This Standard Operating Procedure may be suitably modified with
advance intimation to all the Stake Holders as and when required.
SOP - Pilot Implementation of the Paperless Gujarat High Court Project - eGujHC Project Page 3/3
